what: How each Minnesota place voted in five contests of the 2020, 2022 and 2024 general elections: the votes for the Democratic-Farmer-Labor ticket, the Republican ticket, everyone else together (write-ins included) and the total, added up from the Minnesota Secretary of State's official precinct results.
note: What this is: how the people of a place voted in that election, in the Secretary of State's precinct results as the State Canvassing Board certified them, added up here by county, by city or township and by district, on the precinct and district lines in force at that election. What this is not: it is not a prediction of any election; it says nothing about any candidate on a later ballot or about any voter; a nonpartisan office stays nonpartisan; and a place is not its lines for ever: where land was annexed, a township became a city or a district was redrawn, the figures are for the lines of that year. The tickets are named, as the Secretary's own column definitions name them, only to say which election this was. In a place with very few voters the split would come close to saying how particular people voted; those contests are listed in the place's too_few, and a page should leave the split out.
how_to_read: Each place's votes are four counts for each contest: dfl (the Democratic-Farmer-Labor ticket), rep (the Republican ticket), other (every other candidate and all write-ins) and total. A contest a place does not have was not held on its lines, or the place is newer than that election.

too_few.why: A place's too_few lists the contests in which it had fewer than 20 votes, or in which every vote went the same way. There the split comes close to saying how particular people voted, so a page should leave it out. The counts are the official record all the same, and are kept here so that the sums can be checked.

county.key: five-digit county FIPS code: 27 and the three digits our Minnesota county ids use

mcd.key: five-digit MCD FIPS code, as sl_places kind mcd

senate.what: State Senate districts of the 2022 plan
senate.key: district number, as sl_places kind senate
senate.why_not_2020: These lines were drawn again for the 2022 election, after the census, so a number in the 2020 table need not be the same district, and 2020 is not given.

house.what: State House districts of the 2022 plan
house.key: district number and letter, as sl_places kind house
house.why_not_2020: These lines were drawn again for the 2022 election, after the census, so a number in the 2020 table need not be the same district, and 2020 is not given.

judicial.key: JD and the district number, as sl_places kind judicial

commissioner.key: five-digit county FIPS code, a hyphen, the district number
commissioner.why_not_2020: These lines were drawn again for the 2022 election, after the census, so a number in the 2020 table need not be the same district, and 2020 is not given.
commissioner.note: Numbered within each county as the Secretary's table numbers them in that year.

ward.key: the city's MCD FIPS code, a hyphen, the ward as the table writes it without W- and leading zeros
ward.why_not_2020: These lines were drawn again for the 2022 election, after the census, so a number in the 2020 table need not be the same district, and 2020 is not given.
ward.note: As the Secretary's table writes a precinct's ward (W-01, W-E). A city that names its council seats another way (a district, a section, a precinct, two wards together) is not matched here.

hospital.key: HD and the Secretary's district code in five digits, as sl_places kind hospital
hospital.note: The precincts the Secretary's table puts in the district in that year; 2 of these districts are not in the 2024 table.

control.statement: For every contest the precinct rows add up to the official statewide totals named here; in every precinct the candidates add up to the precinct's own total; and every kind of place that covers the whole state adds up to the statewide sum.

2022-governor.where: the page's table of votes; only each row's party and votes are kept

notes: The Minnesota Legislative Manual 2023-2024, as the Legislative Reference Library archives it (https://www.lrl.mn.gov/archive/sessions/electionresults/2022-11-08-g-man.pdf), reads 1,312,313 and 1,119,906 in the totals row of its Governor table, 36 and 35 fewer than the canvassing report, and the table's first page carries the 2020 presidential figures in its first columns (read from the PDF's text on 2026-10-01). The Secretary's precinct table equals the canvassing report, so the Manual is not the control.
